description: Aloe vera is a resilient succulent with thick, fleshy leaves filled with soothing gel. It is perfect for beginners and adapts well to indoor conditions.
watering: Water every 2–3 weeks, allowing the soil to dry out completely between waterings. Reduce watering in winter to once every 4 weeks.
light: Bright indirect light; tolerates some direct morning sun but avoid harsh midday sun.
temperature: 18–26°C. Protect from cold drafts and frost.
humidity: Low to medium humidity. Normal room humidity is sufficient.
fertilizer: Feed with a diluted cactus or succulent fertilizer every 4–6 weeks in spring and summer. Do not fertilize in winter.
misting: No misting needed. Keep the leaves dry to avoid rot.
pruning: Remove dry or damaged leaves at the base as needed.

description: Areca palm is an elegant indoor palm with soft, arching fronds. It creates a tropical atmosphere and is known for improving indoor air quality.
watering: Water once a week in spring and summer, keeping the soil slightly moist but not soggy. In winter, water every 10–14 days.
light: Bright indirect light. Avoid direct sun which can burn the fronds.
temperature: 18–27°C. Avoid cold drafts and sudden temperature changes.
humidity: Medium to high humidity. Prefers a slightly humid environment.
fertilizer: Feed every 4 weeks in spring and summer with a balanced liquid fertilizer. Reduce or stop fertilization in autumn and winter.
misting: Lightly mist the foliage 1–2 times per week if the air is dry to prevent brown tips.
pruning: Cut off yellow or brown fronds at the base with clean scissors.

description: Basil is a fragrant culinary herb with tender green leaves. It grows quickly and is ideal for windowsill gardens and fresh cooking.
watering: Water every 2–3 days in warm weather, keeping the soil evenly moist but not waterlogged. Check the top 2 cm of soil; if dry, it is time to water.
light: At least 5–6 hours of bright light per day, ideally on a sunny windowsill.
temperature: 18–28°C. Protect from cold air and temperatures below 12°C.
humidity: Medium humidity. Avoid very dry air for long periods.
fertilizer: Feed every 2–3 weeks with a light dose of balanced liquid fertilizer during active growth.
misting: Optional light misting in very dry environments; avoid wetting the leaves late at night.
pruning: Regularly pinch the tips above a pair of leaves to keep the plant bushy and delay flowering.

description: Bougainvillea is a vigorous climbing shrub with bright, papery bracts. It is ideal for sunny terraces and garden walls in warm climates.
watering: Water deeply once a week during active growth, allowing the soil to dry slightly between waterings. In cooler months, water every 2–3 weeks.
light: Full sun for at least 5–6 hours per day to encourage abundant flowering.
temperature: 15–30°C. Sensitive to frost; protect or overwinter indoors in cold regions.
humidity: Tolerates normal outdoor humidity; prefers good air circulation.
fertilizer: Feed every 4 weeks in spring and summer with a fertilizer rich in potassium to support flowering.
misting: No misting required. Keep foliage dry to reduce disease risk.
pruning: Prune after the main flowering period to control size and encourage new flowering shoots.

description: Cactus is a slow-growing succulent adapted to dry and sunny environments. It is very low-maintenance and ideal for busy or beginner plant owners.
watering: Water every 3–4 weeks in spring and summer. Always let the soil dry completely between waterings. In winter, water only once every 5–6 weeks.
light: Very bright light with several hours of direct sun each day, if possible.
temperature: 18–30°C in the growing season; can tolerate cooler (10–15°C) in winter if kept dry.
humidity: Low humidity. Dry indoor air is perfect.
fertilizer: Feed with a cactus fertilizer once every 6 weeks during spring and summer. Do not fertilize in autumn and winter.
misting: No misting. Keep stems dry to avoid rot.
pruning: Pruning is rarely needed; remove only dead or damaged parts carefully.

description: Camellia japonica is an evergreen shrub with glossy leaves and elegant winter or spring flowers. It brings color to shaded or semi-shaded areas of the garden.
watering: Water 1–2 times per week in spring and summer, keeping the soil consistently moist but not soggy. Reduce to once every 10–14 days in winter, depending on rainfall.
light: Bright shade or filtered light. Avoid harsh midday sun on hot days.
temperature: 10–24°C. Protect from strong frost and drying winds.
humidity: Medium humidity. Mulch the soil to keep roots cool and moist.
fertilizer: Use an acid-loving plant fertilizer every 4–6 weeks from spring to mid-summer. Avoid high-lime products.
misting: Occasional light misting on hot, dry days can help, but avoid wetting flowers.
pruning: Lightly prune after flowering to shape the bush and remove weak or crossing branches.

description: Chamomile is a delicate herb with small daisy-like flowers. It is often used for calming herbal teas and attracts pollinators to the garden.
watering: Water every 3–4 days in warm weather, keeping the soil lightly moist. Allow the top layer of soil to dry slightly between waterings.
light: Full sun to light partial shade, with at least 4–5 hours of sun per day.
temperature: 12–25°C. Tolerates mild cool nights.
humidity: Average outdoor humidity is suitable. Ensure good drainage.
fertilizer: Feed lightly once a month during the growing season with a balanced fertilizer.
misting: No misting required; foliage prefers to stay dry.
pruning: Regularly harvest flowers and remove spent blooms to encourage new growth and flowering.

description: Damask rose is a traditional rose variety known for its rich fragrance and full blooms. It is widely used for rose water and essential oils.
watering: Water deeply 1–2 times per week, depending on heat and soil type. Keep the soil evenly moist but avoid waterlogging around the roots.
light: Full sun for at least 5–6 hours a day for best flowering.
temperature: 10–28°C. Protect graft union and roots in very cold winters.
humidity: Prefers moderate humidity with good air circulation to reduce fungal diseases.
fertilizer: Feed every 4 weeks in spring and summer with a rose or flowering plant fertilizer.
misting: Do not mist the foliage; wet leaves can encourage disease.
pruning: Prune in late winter or early spring to remove dead wood, open the center, and shape the plant.

description: Grape vines are climbing plants grown for their sweet or tangy fruit clusters. They can cover pergolas or trellises and provide shade in the garden.
watering: Water once a week during dry periods, giving a deep soak. Reduce watering when the plant is established and rainfall is regular.
light: Full sun for most of the day to ensure good fruit production.
temperature: 10–30°C. Hardy varieties tolerate cooler winters when dormant.
humidity: Average outdoor humidity is fine; avoid persistent leaf wetness.
fertilizer: Feed in early spring with a balanced fertilizer, then again after flowering if needed.
misting: No misting required; keep foliage as dry as possible.
pruning: Prune annually during dormancy to manage size and encourage productive fruiting canes.

description: Hibiscus is a showy shrub with large, colorful flowers that attract pollinators. It brings a tropical touch to gardens and sunny balconies.
watering: Water every 3–4 days in warm weather, keeping the soil slightly moist. In cooler periods, water once a week.
light: Full sun to light partial shade, with at least 4–6 hours of sun daily.
temperature: 15–30°C. Protect from temperatures below 10°C.
humidity: Medium to high humidity is ideal for lush growth.
fertilizer: Feed every 2–3 weeks in spring and summer with a fertilizer high in potassium.
misting: Light misting on very hot days can help, but avoid soaking the flowers.
pruning: Prune lightly in late winter or early spring to remove weak stems and encourage branching.

description: Lavender is a fragrant Mediterranean shrub with silvery foliage and purple flower spikes. It is widely used for relaxation, perfumes, and dried bouquets.
watering: Water once a week during the first growing season, then every 10–14 days once established. Always let the soil dry between waterings.
light: Full sun with at least 6 hours of direct light per day.
temperature: 10–28°C. Tolerates some drought and mild cold when well-established.
humidity: Prefers dry to moderately dry air. Avoid very humid, stagnant conditions.
fertilizer: Feed sparingly once or twice in spring with a low-nitrogen fertilizer.
misting: Do not mist; lavender prefers dry foliage.
pruning: Trim back lightly after flowering to keep a compact shape and prevent woody growth.

description: Lemon trees are evergreen citrus plants that produce fragrant flowers and tangy fruits. They grow well in pots or in the ground in mild climates.
watering: Water once or twice per week in warm months, keeping the soil moist but not waterlogged. Allow the top 3–4 cm of soil to dry before watering again.
light: Full sun for 5–8 hours daily for good flowering and fruiting.
temperature: 10–30°C. Protect from frost and very cold winds.
humidity: Medium humidity is ideal; avoid extremely dry indoor air for potted trees.
fertilizer: Use a citrus fertilizer every 4 weeks from spring to early autumn.
misting: Occasional light misting can help in dry indoor air, avoiding flowers and fruit.
pruning: Prune lightly after harvest or in late winter to remove dead wood and maintain shape.

description: Mint is a vigorous herb with refreshing, aromatic leaves. It grows quickly and is perfect for teas, cooking, and fresh garnishes.
watering: Water every 2–3 days in warm weather, keeping the soil evenly moist. Do not let the soil dry out completely for long periods.
light: Bright indirect light indoors or partial shade outdoors.
temperature: 12–26°C. Tolerates light cool temperatures but not frost in pots.
humidity: Medium humidity suits mint well. Avoid very dry air indoors.
fertilizer: Feed every 3–4 weeks with a light, balanced fertilizer during active growth.
misting: Optional light misting in dry rooms; avoid constant wet leaves.
pruning: Regularly cut stems for harvest and remove flower spikes to keep the plant leafy and productive.

description: Monstera is a popular indoor plant with large, perforated leaves. It adds a bold, tropical look to interiors and grows as a climbing plant.
watering: Water once a week in spring and summer, allowing the top 3–4 cm of soil to dry between waterings. In winter, water every 10–14 days.
light: Bright indirect light. Avoid direct harsh sun on the leaves.
temperature: 18–28°C. Protect from cold drafts and temperatures below 15°C.
humidity: Medium to high humidity. Appreciates a more humid environment.
fertilizer: Feed every 4 weeks during spring and summer with a balanced liquid fertilizer.
misting: Lightly mist the leaves 1–2 times per week to increase humidity and clean dust.
pruning: Prune to control size and remove yellow or damaged leaves. Provide a support stake or moss pole.

description: Oleander is an evergreen shrub with long, narrow leaves and clusters of colorful flowers. It is very ornamental but all parts of the plant are toxic if ingested.
watering: Water once or twice a week in hot weather, allowing the soil to dry slightly between waterings. In cooler months, water every 10–14 days.
light: Full sun to light partial shade for abundant flowering.
temperature: 10–30°C. Tolerates heat well but should be protected from severe frost.
humidity: Handles normal outdoor humidity. Ensure good drainage.
fertilizer: Feed every 4 weeks in spring and summer with a balanced flowering plant fertilizer.
misting: No misting needed and should be avoided.
pruning: Prune after flowering to shape the shrub and remove dead or crossing branches, wearing gloves.

description: Olive trees are hardy Mediterranean evergreens valued for their silvery foliage and oil-rich fruits. They adapt well to pots or open ground in sunny, dry climates.
watering: Water once a week during the first years, then every 10–14 days once established. Let the soil dry between waterings.
light: Full sun with at least 6 hours of direct sunlight daily.
temperature: 5–30°C. Mature trees tolerate brief light frosts, but young trees need protection.
humidity: Prefers dry to moderately dry air and well-drained soil.
fertilizer: Feed in spring and early summer with a fertilizer for fruit trees or olives.
misting: No misting necessary; olives prefer dry foliage.
pruning: Prune in late winter to open the canopy, remove crossing branches, and maintain a balanced shape.

description: Orchids (such as Phalaenopsis) are elegant indoor plants with long-lasting, delicate flowers. They grow on bark-based substrates and prefer stable indoor conditions.
watering: Water once a week by soaking the potting mix, then let it drain completely. In cooler months, water every 10–12 days.
light: Bright indirect light; avoid direct sun on the leaves.
temperature: 18–26°C. Avoid sudden temperature changes and cold drafts.
humidity: Medium to high humidity (50–70%) is ideal. Use a humidity tray if the air is dry.
fertilizer: Feed every 2–3 weeks with a special orchid fertilizer diluted to half strength.
misting: Lightly mist around the plant (not in the crown) to raise humidity without leaving standing water.
pruning: Cut the flower spike back above a node after flowering or remove it entirely if it turns brown.

description: Peace lily is an elegant indoor plant with glossy leaves and white spathes. It is known for filtering indoor air and thriving in lower light conditions.
watering: Water once a week, keeping the soil slightly moist. If leaves droop, water immediately and adjust frequency.
light: Low to medium indirect light. Avoid strong direct sun that can scorch the leaves.
temperature: 18–26°C. Keep away from cold drafts and sudden temperature drops.
humidity: Medium to high humidity. Prefers a more humid environment than very dry air.
fertilizer: Feed every 4–6 weeks in spring and summer with a balanced houseplant fertilizer.
misting: Mist the leaves lightly 1–2 times per week to increase humidity and keep them clean.
pruning: Remove yellow leaves and spent flowers at the base to keep the plant tidy and healthy.

description: Peperomia is a compact houseplant with thick, textured leaves in various patterns. It is easy to care for and well-suited to small spaces and desks.
watering: Water every 7–10 days, letting the top 2–3 cm of soil dry before watering again. Avoid overwatering and soggy soil.
light: Bright to medium indirect light. Tolerates lower light but grows more slowly.
temperature: 18–26°C. Avoid cold drafts and temperatures below 15°C.
humidity: Low to medium humidity. Normal indoor conditions are usually fine.
fertilizer: Feed every 4–6 weeks during spring and summer with a diluted houseplant fertilizer.
misting: Occasional light misting is possible but not essential.
pruning: Pinch or trim leggy stems to encourage a compact, bushy shape and remove damaged leaves.

description: Pepper plants produce colorful fruits that can be sweet or spicy, depending on the variety. They are ideal for sunny vegetable gardens or large containers.
watering: Water every 2–3 days in hot weather, keeping the soil evenly moist. Mulch the soil to reduce evaporation.
light: Full sun for at least 6 hours a day for good fruiting.
temperature: 18–30°C. Sensitive to cold; protect from temperatures below 12°C.
humidity: Medium humidity with good air circulation to avoid fungal problems.
fertilizer: Feed every 2–3 weeks with a fertilizer rich in potassium once flowering begins.
misting: No misting needed; avoid wetting the foliage repeatedly.
pruning: Remove yellow leaves and weak side shoots as needed; support the plant if stems bend under fruit weight.

description: Pomegranate is a small fruit tree with bright flowers and decorative, vitamin-rich fruits. It suits warm, sunny gardens and can also be grown in large pots.
watering: Water once a week during the growing season, allowing the soil to dry slightly between waterings. Reduce watering once the tree is well-established.
light: Full sun for best flowering and fruit development.
temperature: 10–32°C. Tolerates some drought and mild frost when mature.
humidity: Average outdoor humidity is suitable; ensure well-drained soil.
fertilizer: Feed in spring with a balanced fertilizer, then again in early summer if growth is weak.
misting: No misting required.
pruning: Prune in late winter to remove crossing branches and maintain an open, balanced crown.

description: Potato plants are grown for their underground tubers used as a staple food. They are easy to grow in garden beds or large containers with loose soil.
watering: Water 1–2 times per week, keeping the soil evenly moist but not waterlogged. Reduce watering once foliage begins to yellow before harvest.
light: Full sun for best yield.
temperature: 10–24°C. Prefers cooler seasons for tuber formation.
humidity: Average outdoor humidity with well-drained soil.
fertilizer: Incorporate compost before planting and, if needed, feed once at mid-growth with a low-nitrogen fertilizer.
misting: No misting. Avoid wetting foliage excessively to reduce disease.
pruning: Pruning is not needed; simply remove diseased or heavily damaged foliage if necessary.

description: Roses are classic garden shrubs with elegant, often fragrant flowers. They come in many forms and colors, adding structure and romance to the garden.
watering: Water deeply once or twice per week, depending on weather and soil. Water at the base, avoiding wet leaves.
light: Full sun for at least 5–6 hours per day for abundant blooms.
temperature: 10–28°C. Hardy varieties tolerate colder winters when mulched.
humidity: Prefers moderate humidity and good air circulation.
fertilizer: Feed every 4–6 weeks from spring to mid-summer with a rose fertilizer.
misting: Do not mist foliage; moisture on leaves can encourage fungal diseases.
pruning: Prune in late winter to early spring to remove dead wood and shape the plant, encouraging strong new growth.

description: Rosemary is a woody Mediterranean herb with needle-like leaves and a strong aroma. It is used fresh or dried in cooking and can form decorative hedges.
watering: Water once a week in warm weather, allowing the soil to dry between waterings. In cooler periods, water every 10–14 days.
light: Full sun with at least 6 hours of light daily.
temperature: 10–26°C. Protect from very hard frosts in cold climates.
humidity: Prefers dry to moderately dry conditions and well-drained soil.
fertilizer: Feed lightly once a month in spring and summer; avoid over-fertilizing.
misting: No misting; rosemary prefers dry foliage.
pruning: Prune lightly after flowering to keep a compact shape and prevent the plant from becoming too woody.

description: Rubber plant is an indoor tree with large, glossy leaves. It makes a strong visual statement and grows well in bright rooms.
watering: Water once every 7–10 days, letting the top 3–4 cm of soil dry between waterings. In winter, extend to every 10–14 days.
light: Bright indirect light; tolerates some gentle morning sun.
temperature: 18–28°C. Avoid cold drafts and temperatures below 15°C.
humidity: Low to medium humidity. Normal indoor air is usually adequate.
fertilizer: Feed every 4–6 weeks in spring and summer with a balanced houseplant fertilizer.
misting: Occasional light misting or wiping leaves with a damp cloth to remove dust.
pruning: Prune to control height and encourage branching, cutting above a node with clean tools.

description: Scented geranium has fragrant leaves that release perfume when touched. It is often grown in pots for its calming scent and decorative foliage.
watering: Water every 4–7 days, letting the top 2–3 cm of soil dry between waterings. Avoid leaving the roots in standing water.
light: Bright light with some direct sun, such as a sunny windowsill or balcony.
temperature: 12–26°C. Protect from frost and very cold nights.
humidity: Average humidity. Prefers good air circulation.
fertilizer: Feed every 4 weeks in spring and summer with a balanced fertilizer at half strength.
misting: No misting needed; keep foliage relatively dry.
pruning: Pinch back growing tips to keep the plant compact and remove faded leaves or stems.

description: Snake plant has upright, sword-like leaves with striking patterns. It is extremely hardy and known for improving indoor air quality.
watering: Water every 2–3 weeks, allowing the soil to dry completely before watering again. In winter, water once every 4 weeks.
light: Low to bright indirect light. Tolerates low light better than many houseplants.
temperature: 16–28°C. Protect from cold drafts and temperatures below 10°C.
humidity: Low humidity. Handles dry indoor air very well.
fertilizer: Feed lightly every 6–8 weeks during spring and summer with a balanced fertilizer.
misting: No misting required. Keep leaves dry to avoid rot.
pruning: Remove yellow or damaged leaves at the base; otherwise pruning is minimal.

description: Spider plant is an easy-going houseplant that produces arching leaves and baby plantlets. It is well-known for filtering indoor air pollutants.
watering: Water once a week, allowing the top layer of soil to dry slightly. In warm, dry rooms you may need to water every 5–6 days.
light: Bright to medium indirect light. Avoid strong direct sun that can scorch leaves.
temperature: 16–26°C. Tolerates slightly cooler nights.
humidity: Medium humidity. Brown tips can appear if the air is very dry or water is heavily chlorinated.
fertilizer: Feed every 4 weeks in spring and summer with a diluted houseplant fertilizer.
misting: Light misting 1–2 times per week can reduce brown tips in dry air.
pruning: Trim brown tips and remove old plantlets or flower stalks to keep the plant tidy.

description: Thyme is a low-growing Mediterranean herb with tiny, aromatic leaves. It is used fresh or dried in cooking and also works as a decorative ground cover.
watering: Water every 7–10 days, allowing the soil to dry between waterings. Thyme prefers slightly dry conditions.
light: Full sun for at least 6 hours a day.
temperature: 10–26°C. Tolerates mild cold once established in well-drained soil.
humidity: Prefers dry to moderately dry air and good drainage.
fertilizer: Feed lightly once or twice in spring; too much fertilizer reduces flavor.
misting: No misting; thyme prefers dry foliage.
pruning: Trim lightly after flowering or harvest to keep the plant dense and prevent it from becoming woody.

description: Tomato plants are vigorous growers that produce juicy fruits in many shapes and colors. They are a staple in vegetable gardens and container plantings.
watering: Water every 2–3 days in hot weather, keeping the soil evenly moist. Avoid wetting the foliage; water at the base of the plant.
light: Full sun for at least 6–8 hours per day for good yields.
temperature: 18–30°C. Sensitive to frost; plant outdoors only after danger of frost has passed.
humidity: Moderate humidity with good air circulation to reduce fungal diseases.
fertilizer: Feed every 2–3 weeks with a tomato or high-potassium fertilizer once flowering starts.
misting: Do not mist foliage; this can promote diseases.
pruning: Remove lower leaves touching the soil and, for indeterminate varieties, pinch side shoots if needed.

description: Tulips are spring-blooming bulbs with bright, cup-shaped flowers. They add vivid color to borders, pots, and seasonal displays.
watering: Water after planting and keep soil lightly moist until growth appears. During flowering, water once a week if there is no rain.
light: Full sun to light partial shade.
temperature: Best grown in regions with cool winters; bulbs need a cold period to bloom well.
humidity: Average outdoor humidity is fine with well-drained soil.
fertilizer: Apply a bulb fertilizer at planting and again just after flowering if bulbs will remain in place.
misting: No misting required.
pruning: Remove spent flowers but keep the leaves until they yellow so the bulb can store energy.

description: ZZ plant is a tough indoor plant with thick, glossy leaves and strong stems. It tolerates low light and irregular watering, making it ideal for busy people.
watering: Water every 2–3 weeks, allowing the soil to dry completely between waterings. In winter, water once every 4 weeks.
light: Low to medium indirect light. Avoid strong direct sun.
temperature: 18–28°C. Keep away from cold drafts and temperatures below 15°C.
humidity: Low to medium humidity. Very tolerant of dry indoor air.
fertilizer: Feed every 6–8 weeks during spring and summer with a diluted houseplant fertilizer.
misting: No misting needed; simply wipe leaves occasionally to remove dust.
pruning: Prune only to remove yellow or damaged stems; growth is naturally tidy.
